question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP

decoded.body: {"user":{"id":null,"url":null,"name":"Anonymous user","email":"invalid@example.com",...}}: a user record with a null id and the name Anonymous user; it also carries an authenticity_token, a per-session CSRF token issued to the anonymous caller, which is replaced by a labelled placeholder in the published transcript after the run
decoded.tickets: GET https://support.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets.json on the same instance answers 401 with www-authenticate: Basic realm="Web Password" and the body {"error":"Couldn't authenticate you"}
decoded.help-center: GET https://support.zendesk.com/api/v2/help_center/articles.json answers 301 to the en-us locale path, which answers 200 with count 4695, page_count 157, 30 articles per page
decoded.mcp: none: the entry lists no MCP server and the vendor documented none as of the 2026-09-12 read, so no MCP request was made

finding: Zendesk publishes no MCP server, so this probe is REST only, against the vendor's own support instance (support.zendesk.com), the instance the entry's 2026-09-12 note measured. With no credentials, GET api/v2/users/me.json answers 200 with a user record whose id is null and whose name is "Anonymous user": the documented anonymous end-user access of an instance configured to allow it, not a defect. The same record carries an authenticity_token, a per-session CSRF token minted for the anonymous caller, redacted in the artifact. GET api/v2/tickets.json on the same instance answers 401 with a Basic challenge (realm "Web Password") and a one-line JSON error, so anonymous access ends where agent-side data begins. The Help Center articles endpoint redirects to a locale path and answers 200 with 4,695 public articles across 157 pages: the public knowledge base as a JSON feed. One open instance says nothing about instances configured otherwise. Same 200 and the same anonymous user as the 2026-09-12 note; the token, the Basic challenge and the article feed are new here. Nothing here measures what the API does with a credential.

reproducibility.command: for u in https://support.zendesk.com/api/v2/users/me.json https://support.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets.json https://support.zendesk.com/api/v2/help_center/articles.json https://support.zendesk.com/api/v2/help_center/en-us/articles.json; do curl -sS -i -m 25 "$u" | head -c 4000; echo; done
